_note: Two independent judges, S245 (20/10/2026). Criteria scored 1-5: quality_gain, safety, cost, time_to_value, operability. Judge 1 took Ms. Thư's / product lens; judge 2 the engineering / safety lens and spot-checked the schema dump.

judges.lens: product owner (Ms. Thư) + time to visible value

scores.why: One loop covers A1, T2 and T9 and attacks what Ms. Thư sees: recurring errors (rules from gate_ledger, repair_log and audit_log admin_sentence_* before/after) and tenant voice (k=3 tenant-filtered, entity-masked exemplars replacing the static good_examples slot). Reuses existing injection points, so the first release reaches all writers around session 4 of ~6 with no prompt refactor. Constraint-only lint, B-class hard stop, RLS + 5-gram guard, pointer-flip rollback. Lowest cost ($30-50/month). Loses a point on operability: four new tables, a five-tab page and auto-promoted tenant releases for one reviewer. Spot-check confirmed: flag_fix_node.py L733 writes stage='audit'; s1_batch.py L112 and admin_pipeline.py L565 read S1_rewrite/S1_editor; dump L4290 shows 0 inserts and 1,956 index scans.

Strongest safety (locked fidelity slots, DB trigger requiring a passing holdout, kappa >= 0.6 judges, byte-identical R0 replay, public-repo rule, offboarding deletion). Worst time to value: golden sets, calibrated judges (AA-729, AA-783) and a slot refactor come before any optimiser candidate; first automated improvement in P3 (~sessions 5-7 of 7-8). Voice learning late. GEPA campaigns $10-25 each, up to $70/month. Writer Lab plus nine tables heavy for one reviewer.

L0 lexicon is the cheapest visible win; lessons, exemplars and CIPHER tenant summary target voice; nothing auto-activates. But carries scope a product owner does not need now (preference pairs, SFT/DPO export to S3, readiness meter, GEPA spike, conditional fine-tune) and raises tenant-consent/legal questions for Ms. Thư. Lessons land ~session 3.5. Highest monthly cost ($35-80).

flaws_in_winner: Time to value hinges on AA-729; no lexicon-only fast path.
Tenant voice learning likely empty on Dev with 4 synthetic tenants and one reviewer; platform rules in practice only from the >= 5% gate-recurrence route.
Dev-phase auto-promotion of tenant releases; fidelity gate leans on uncalibrated AA-803 and unbuilt AA-845 reject truth.
approval_basis tenant_final_edit relies on fidelity filter + masking; residual masking risk unmeasured.
minutes_to_fix and light-edit KPIs depend on labels that barely exist.
Operational surface for one reviewer; <= 30 min/week asserted, not evidenced.
Unknowns: T2 stamp column, audit_log sentence-edit volume, current T2 unit cost, prompt caching on acc3.
Cost estimate omits forced R2 reruns from AA-787 gate rename and route/model changes.

scores.why: Reuses existing injection points (lessons append verified at s1_batch.py L108-121, render_brand_block good_examples, _repair_feedback, AA-800 layers); no slot refactor. Strongest safety design: constraint-only lint, adds_unsourced_claim quarantine, entity-masked 'style only' exemplars, scope CHECK, no aa_app_user grant, isolation probe as hard stop, activation refused by CHECK without eval and shadow, pointer-flip rollback. Correctly spots the trap: T2 runs the S1 graph (stages.py stage_for, AA-763, verified), so fixing the stage mismatch (flag_fix_node.py L733, verified) would leak tenant text into a global prompt. Per-rule attribution via rule_ids stamps. Loses points: no kappa anchor, tenant auto-promotion, a few schema errors.

Best eval discipline (first-class golden tables, holdout, per-item results, kappa >= 0.6, candidate funnel, edit-pair replay KPI, public-repo rule, offboarding lifecycle). But its spine is a refactor of all writer/repair prompts into DB-resolved slots with a wide blast radius (shared graph), ~8 new/altered tables, and a GEPA-lite optimiser that needs a full valset pass per candidate on very thin data (OPRO-style overfitting regime). 7-8 sessions; heavy weekly campaign cadence for one reviewer.

Solid P0 (same-transaction record_writer_feedback, source_audit_id uuid matching audit_log.id, async fidelity_status). Honest about vendor churn. But widest scope (six layers, preference pairs, CIPHER, GEPA spike, SFT/DPO JSONL exports to S3, cross-region fine-tune) adds a tenant-text-at-rest surface not needed now; fine-tuning effectively unavailable; 'nothing auto-activates' makes the single reviewer the bottleneck; $35-80/month; less rigorous release/attribution (rule_set_version hash).

flaws_in_winner: Schema: writing_signal.audit_log_id declared bigint but acp_shared.audit_log.id is uuid; audit_log.tenant_id is varchar(50), not uuid.
No place to stamp memory_release_id on T2: tenant_tour_versions has no metadata or writer_input column (only rewritten_content jsonb) -> needs a nullable generation_meta jsonb migration.
Tenant-scope auto-promotion in dev = promotion on noise; per DM-11.5 the first paid tenant/prod must switch to a human click; ADR should state it as a dated invariant.
Eval combinatorics (6 writer keys + stacked tenant layers) can exceed $15/run and $30-50/month; needs a monthly budget and R2 limited to affected strata.
Statistical power: <= 50 paired items will mostly be inconclusive; needs a 'non-inferior on hard stops + directional gain, pooled across rounds' fallback.
Hard dependency on AA-729; decouple P0 and R0 lexicon rules to ship value earlier.
Tenant text duplicated into shared tables needs RLS + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or an explicit cis_app-only model with code-side filtering; the option does not say whether cis_app bypasses RLS.
Effort likely understated: plan for ~8 sessions, not 6.
ADR numbering: an app ADR '0009' collides by name with the reserved ecosystem ADR 0009 (AI platform, AA-804); use a distinct title and cite it.
